title: NetTAG: A Multimodal RTL-and-Layout-Aligned Netlist Foundation Model via Text-Attributed Graph
problem: Circuit representation learning methods rely on complex functional supervision (truth-table simulation) and handle only simple-and-inverter graphs, failing to encode diverse gate functionalities and lacking structural awareness needed for full netlist understanding.
motivation: Advancing Electronic Design Automation requires circuit representations that capture both gate-level semantics and global structure, bridging the gap between LLM functional understanding and graph-based structural learning.
method: NetTAG formulates netlists as text-attributed graphs with gates annotated by symbolic logic expressions and physical characteristics, combining an LLM-based text encoder for gate semantics and a graph transformer for structure; pre-trained with self-supervised objectives and aligned to RTL and layout stages.
key_novelty: Multimodal text-attributed graph representation of netlists fusing LLM-based gate semantics with graph transformer structure learning, supporting both functional and physical design tasks.
contributions: NetTAG netlist foundation model combining text and graph modalities for gate and structure understanding
Text-attributed graph formulation with symbolic logic expressions for gate semantics
Multimodal architecture with LLM text encoder and graph transformer backbone
Outperforms task-specific methods on four diverse functional and physical tasks

metrics.accuracy: Outperforms task-specific methods on four different functional and physical tasks

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation on multiple EDA tasks without detailed task-specific performance metrics.
primary_theme: Multimodal text-attributed graph netlist foundation model for EDA
